statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 4, low, because CME equity index futures have been halted since Friday at 21:00Z and eighteen of the twenty-four hours published here contain no tradable interval at all; only the six slots from the scheduled 22:00Z Sunday reopen onward are tradable, and they carry conditional Tail readings of 12, 13, 12, 11, 10 and 10 that stay far below the block threshold. Stress is 35, moderate: the 50% US tariff on about $20 billion of Canadian goods is in force after trade talks collapsed, Canada has dated a dollar-for-dollar match to 8 September, a Monday US press conference on Iran economic isolation is scheduled, the thirty-year Treasury yield sits at 5.23% near post-2007 highs, and energy has gained roughly 5% for a second consecutive week, all of it unpriced until the venue reopens. Confidence is 87, high: levels, yields, oil, volatility, catalysts and the seven-day calendar are all verified and current, and the absence of a live price path is a known market state rather than a gap in the evidence.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than a one-way path: cash NDX opened at 29,359.60, traded down to 29,142.44, recovered to 29,405.12 and closed at 29,308.86, up 0.33% on the day and below its own open, ending a five-day losing streak, while the VIX settled at 14.89 near the low of a 14.77-15.95 range. Both session extremes were retraced and neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, so no Tail amplifier carries over from observed structure. Friday internals were split rather than aligned, with application and infrastructure software up about 1.2% against semiconductors down 0.31%, and cross-asset direction was mixed, with gold higher, energy higher and Treasury futures lower. Mapped policy state remains EA_ON across the whole horizon. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers the 22:00Z Sunday reopen through 02:00Z Monday, where a static weekend information set would be expressed in one auction into thin liquidity; that is gap and scenario exposure, not observed structure, and a later run will score the actual path once it prints.
headline: Closed-venue assessment with six reopen hours inside the horizon: Tail holds the floor of 4 through eighteen shut hours, then carries conditional readings of 12, 13, 12, 11, 10 and 10 from the 22:00Z Sunday reopen, while live US tariffs on Canadian goods, a scheduled Monday Iran economic-isolation announcement, a post-2007 long end and a second week of energy gains stay unpriced.
body: CME Globex equity index futures stopped trading for the week on Friday at 21:00Z and are scheduled to reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z. The twenty-four slots published here run from 2026-08-23T04:00:00Z to 2026-08-24T03:00:00Z, so the reopen slot and the first five hours after it sit inside the horizon. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86 on Friday, up 0.33% from a 29,213.17 prior close, after opening at 29,359.60 and printing a 29,142.44 low and a 29,405.12 high; both extremes were retraced inside the session, the close finished below the open, and the day ended a five-day losing streak even as the Nasdaq lost about 2% on the week in a Treasury-led selloff. The VIX settled at 14.89, down 6.0%, near the low of a 14.77-15.95 range. On policy, the 50% US tariff on roughly $20 billion of Canadian goods took effect after Friday midnight once talks collapsed, and Prime Minister Carney has said Canada will match it dollar for dollar from 8 September across steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp, paper and electronics; both governments have framed the breakdown as unresolved rather than a pause. The Treasury secretary's Monday press conference detailing an Iran economic-isolation plan covering exchange houses, ship registries and oil smuggling routes remains scheduled and unheld. On rates, the 20 August H.15 column shows two years at 4.19%, ten years at 4.69% and thirty years at 5.23%, with the long end near post-2007 highs after touching 5.33% on 18 August; that repricing has been the dominant equity headwind of the month but cannot transmit while the venue is shut. Energy closed the week with WTI at $87.06 and Brent at $94.39 after a second consecutive weekly gain of roughly 5%, with reporting noting signs that Iran may be seeking an end to the conflict. Delayed latest-session cross-asset context is consistent with that picture and shows no aligned one-way alignment. Because no Nasdaq-100 interval exists in eighteen of these twenty-four hours, Tail holds its closed-venue floor of 4 through them; the six tradable slots carry conditional gap-and-scenario readings that peak at 13 in the first full hour after the reopen and decay to 10 as Tokyo, Hong Kong and mainland liquidity join. Stress is the field that carries the weekend: it eases to 34 through the quiet European hours, rebuilds through the Sunday afternoon headline window, peaks at 53 at the reopen auction and decays to 42 by the end of the horizon. The week ahead is dense, with July PCE and the second Q2 GDP estimate and Nvidia results on Wednesday and the Jackson Hole symposium with the Fed chair keynote on Friday, but those are dated checkpoints in the events array rather than observed structure.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is nearly complete: 21 hourly assessments are available, while the 05:00Z, 06:00Z and 21:00Z clock-hours on 22 August have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across every available hour Tail held 4 and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON, so no hour approached the block threshold and the dominant mode remained normal throughout. Stress traced a shallow arc across the shut weekend: 36 at the start of the window, a build to 42 through Saturday afternoon as the Canadian response was dated and the Iran announcement was scheduled, then a steady easing back to 36 and now 35 as the same static stack aged without new escalation. Confidence held in a narrow 85 to 88 band for the whole window, reflecting evidence that is complete for a closed market and refreshed each hour against primary sources. No hour in the lookback contained a tradable Nasdaq-100 interval, so none of it constitutes observed price-path evidence.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. The following seventeen slots describe the same closed market, so Tail holds 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout them, while Stress dips to 34 through the quiet European hours and then rebuilds to 47 by the last shut hour as the reopen approaches with the information set unchanged. The final six slots are tradable: the 22:00Z scheduled reopen carries a conditional Tail of 12, the first full hour after it the horizon peak of 13, the hour coinciding with the Monday Tokyo cash open a conditional 12, and the last three slots 11, 10 and 10 as Hong Kong and mainland liquidity join. All of those readings rest on gap and thin-liquidity scenarios rather than on observed structure, and all remain green. The invalidation to watch in a later run is the opposite of what is assumed here: shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension and NQ holding near a session extreme after the auction would be genuine Tail evidence, and none of it has been observed.
